findings.description: The first `readSync` asks for `PLAIN_FILE_MAX_BYTES + 1` (1048577) bytes. Linux's pagemap refuses any read whose length is not a multiple of 8 with EINVAL, so `readPlainFile('/proc/self/pagemap')` throws `EINVAL: invalid argument, read` rather than 'is not a plain file'. The new pagemap test therefore fails on every Linux `pnpm test`; it is skipped on macOS, where the gate ran.
findings.body:
**On Linux, the pagemap read fails with EINVAL before it reaches the size cap, so the new test fails there**

`readPlainFile` sizes its buffer one byte past the cap, so its first read asks for 1,048,577 bytes:

```ts
const buffer = Buffer.alloc(PLAIN_FILE_MAX_BYTES + 1);
let length = 0;
for (let read = -1; read !== 0 && length < buffer.length; length += read) {
  read = readSync(fd, buffer, length, buffer.length - length, null);
}
```

Linux's `pagemap_read` (`fs/proc/task_mmu.c`) checks alignment before it walks any page: `if ((*ppos % PM_ENTRY_BYTES) || (count % PM_ENTRY_BYTES)) goto out_mm;` with `ret = -EINVAL`. `PM_ENTRY_BYTES` is 8, and 1048577 % 8 = 1. With `position: null`, Node's `readSync` passes the length to `read(2)` unchanged. So the call throws `EINVAL: invalid argument, read`, and the `is not a plain file` throw is never reached.

Production stays bounded, because every caller catches the error. But:

- On Linux, the test `stops at the size cap on a procfs file that reports size 0` (`capability-utils.test.ts` L130-135, `toThrow('is not a plain file')`) fails on every `pnpm test`. That includes a developer's run, a pup session and a merge gate. On macOS `/proc` is absent and `it.runIf` skips the test, which is why the gate report shows it passing.
- Decision 96's Tests line says the read "stops at the cap ... on `/proc/self/pagemap` where there is one" (`docs/09-decisions.md` ~L5229-5231). The JSDoc says the same. Neither holds on Linux.

This claim rests on kernel and libuv behaviour that can't be read in-tree, so it is medium confidence. Running the test once on a Linux box would settle it.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/6c43b73ba88d4d6e8a7252acdea330ddf1de0d38/src/adapters/capability.utils.ts#L27-L31
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/6c43b73ba88d4d6e8a7252acdea330ddf1de0d38/src/adapters/capability-utils.test.ts#L130-L135

**Fix.** Size the buffer 8 bytes past the cap instead of 1. Every read length then stays a multiple of 8 for pagemap, and `length > PLAIN_FILE_MAX_BYTES` still catches an oversized file. A regular file of exactly 1 MiB still reads whole.
findings.suggestion:
// procfs pagemap refuses a read that is not a multiple of 8 bytes.
    const buffer = Buffer.alloc(PLAIN_FILE_MAX_BYTES + 8);

findings.description: A plain `sh -c` script that starts with a wrapper or env assignment keeps that word in the guard pattern as required text, so the guard misses the command as a session types it. For example, `test: exec pytest "$@"` compiles to `exec[[:space:]]+pytest`, which does not match `pytest tests/x.py`, and `CI=1 go test ./...` misses `go test ./...`. `COMMAND_START` already makes those prefixes optional, so leading `VAR=value`/`exec`/`env`/`command` words could be dropped before escaping.

A multi-word script's pattern still ends in `([[:space:]]|$)`, so the guard misses it when a separator touches the last word with no space: `(cd pkg && go test ./...)`, `go test ./...;echo`, `go test ./...|tail`. `BARE_COMMAND_END` already lists those characters for one-word scripts, so ending multi-word patterns with `([[:space:];&|)`<>]|$)` would make the two cases consistent.

Two mechanisms keep a line break out of `ownTestCommandPattern`. The argv branch checks `/[\r\n\0]/` explicitly, while the `sh -c` branch relies on `PLAIN_SCRIPT` happening to exclude line breaks. If `PLAIN_SCRIPT` is loosened later, blank pattern lines that refuse every Bash call could come back without anyone noticing. Hoisting the `/[\r\n\0]/` check over both branches would keep that guarantee in one place.

`readPlainFile` follows links by default, so every reader of a file only pup writes has to remember to pass `{ followLinks: false }`; two do today, and a forgotten flag silently follows a planted link. If a third such reader lands, flip the default or add a named wrapper for pup-owned files.

The new `vi.mock('node:fs', …)` wrapping `fstatSync` goes against testing.md §"When `vi.mock` is right", which reserves `vi.mock` for tmux panes and `claude -p` sessions ("That is the whole current list"). The mock is also declared after the `./capability.utils.js` import, the reverse of the order the doc asks for. Consider a real file that reports less than it holds, or injecting the stat, instead.

Decision 96 lines edited in this round break the file's ~100-column wrap. Lines 5191, 5213 and 5245 each run well past 100 columns, for example 'beyond plain words, `"$@"` alone or a blank one gets no pattern and lets `git status` through. Launch and `pup new` refuse at the cap…'. The guard paragraph also leaves a short ragged line, 'line break) gets no pattern. A'. Reflow these paragraphs.
